claim.value: Repeated elimination may discard only history incompatible with the classification under the single-transition assumption.
claim.scope: Restriction on which revision history the procedure eliminates.

provenance.rationale: The cited span explicitly supplies both the elimination restriction and its single-transition assumption.

signal_basis.value: Repeated representative midpoint tests produce good, bad or inconclusive classifications against prespecified tail-rate evidence criteria. Confident classifications update the corresponding endpoint; inconclusive results warrant further trials within budget, not elimination based on a single fast export. Repeated-testing rules control accumulated decision error.
signal_basis.scope: Midpoint classification and endpoint updates after endpoints are established, under the single-transition assumption.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the repeated midpoint tests, classification criteria, endpoint updates, elimination assumption and safeguards for inconclusive results and repeated decisions.
No additional unresolved empirical relation is required for this explicitly bounded procedural restriction.

rationale: Under a single transition between established good and bad endpoints, a confidently classified midpoint excludes only transition locations incompatible with that classification. The operation therefore licenses the stated restriction on elimination.
uncertainty: Classification remains subject to its prespecified statistical uncertainty; the claim does not assert error-free localization or validity when the single-transition assumption fails.
